passages.note: These are the projections from the iterated pullback. isoObjects is the selected pair of objects; no comparison with the endpoints of isoArrow is proved by these projection definitions alone.

passages.title: A lift to the isomorphism category
passages.note: Both implications are proved, retaining the comparison to the given arrow and the endpoint-framed inverse triangles. The expression variants allow arbitrary absolute parameter categories.

passages.title: Identity morphisms are invertible
passages.note: This theorem concerns absolute objects. The following identityIso construction supplies a functor C → Iso(C).

passages.title: Two constant triangles with a common edge
The diagonal square representing identifications
passages.note: This is the diagonal-square ingredient derived from the fiber-square assumption, with normalized matching (id, ε). It does not include the subsequent replacement by Iso(C).

passages.title: The Rezk equivalence used in the fiber comparison
passages.note: The comparison is an equivalence of the full specified pullbacks, using the actual endpoint map of isoArrow.

passages.title: Factor the identity-arrow functor
passages.note: This proves the factorization, not the embedding conclusion, which also needs the preceding embedding lemma.

passages.title: The first factor is an equivalence
passages.note: Compose the Rezk equivalence with the embedding of isomorphisms into arrows.

passages.title: The core of the walking triangle
The two-point category is an anima
passages.note: The formalization derives the primitive anima predicate after recognition in Section 2.5. Before recognition it uses the interval-core equivalence and the induced core-inclusion equivalence. The manuscript regards being an anima as invariant under equivalence from Chapter 1.

passages.title: Independence of the composition choice
passages.note: Apply the generic comparison with parameter category Composable C and the whole short-edge comparisons of the chosen triangles.

passages.title: Isomorphisms embed into arrows
passages.note: This proof uses the Segal and square axioms, before the Rezk axiom. It retains the matchings in the successive pullback comparisons.

passages.title: Groupoids
passages.note: The lift is quantified over arbitrary absolute categories of parameters. Contextual inheritance of the entire underlined statement is outside the formalization scope.

passages.title: The terminal category is a groupoid
Pullbacks of groupoids over a category
passages.note: The code compares the cospans induced by constant arrows and by endpoint evaluation, then uses the specified functor-pullback comparison. It proves the same result for an arbitrary common target, without identifying its proof with the manuscript’s displayed factorization through the diagonal of the embedding.

passages.title: The empty category is a groupoid
The core inclusion is an embedding
Initial category and coproducts of animae
The elementary Yoneda criterion
passages.note: The proof applies to absolute morphisms and tests composition on hom categories. Neither Rezk nor recognition is a parameter.

passages.title: Functoriality of cores
passages.note: Postcomposition is specialized at the terminal source. The naturality equation is exposed in CoreInclusions.

passages.title: Cores preserve products
passages.note: Specialize the mapping-anima product comparison to the terminal source.

passages.title: Cores preserve pullbacks
passages.note: Specialize preservation by mapping animae to the terminal source.

passages.title: Cores preserve embeddings
passages.note: Specialize preservation of embeddings by Map(T,-) to the terminal source.

passages.title: Membership in a morphism collection
passages.note: Membership includes the specified identification with the image in the mapping anima.

passages.title: The subcategory axiom
passages.note: The interface assumes the factorization form of the first clause. Its equivalence form is derived as SubcategoryPresentation.first-clause.

passages.title: The generated inclusion is a subcategory
Laws of subcategory functoriality
passages.note: Partial coverage: uniqueness, identification invariance, identities and composition are checked. Preservation of equivalences of both the ambient categories and their morphism collections is not yet linked to a completed theorem.

passages.title: The subcategory spanned by a collection
Spanned subcategories are full
passages.note: The checked proof uses family factorization and the embedding pullback criterion to establish the stated square.

passages.title: Characterization of full subcategories
passages.note: The tested pullback is the displayed square for the chosen collection of objects.

passages.title: The full subcategory on all objects
passages.note: The formal proof uses recovery from all morphisms and equivalences on endpoint maps. The manuscript instead uses the mapping-anima characterization.

passages.title: Pullbacks of full subcategories
passages.note: The formal proof uses universal-family factorization and the embedding pullback criterion. The manuscript tests mapping animae and pastes a cube.

passages.title: Detecting equivalence of a full subcategory
Functors into groupoids invert every morphism
Geometric realizations are animae
passages.note: Despite its historical TeX label, this is a derived proposition, not an additional axiom.

passages.title: Base change of functors over a base
Dependent products preserve embeddings
passages.note: The formal proof is direct, using relative currying and the embedding criterion. It does not use preservation of pullbacks, whose formal proof remains incomplete.

passages.title: Evaluation into a relative functor category
passages.note: This is the universal property for a fixed structural functor to the base. A separate theorem packaging all pairs of structural functors and relative maps is not exported.

passages.title: Base change and fibers of relative functor categories
Mapping animae as cores of global sections
The mapping-out join axiom
passages.note: The mapping-out axiom assumes that the base is an anima.

passages.title: Joins forming a triangle
passages.note: The formal comparisons point from the triangle to the joins; their inverses give the displayed direction.

passages.title: The mapping-out action on joins
passages.note: Partial coverage: this constructs the manuscript action and its full cocone compatibility. Identity and composition laws are currently proved for a separate dependent-product action in JoinFunctoriality; agreement of the two actions is not yet proved.

passages.title: The mapping-in join axiom
passages.note: This is the absolute axiom parametrized by an arbitrary base category. The link does not assert full categorical-context inheritance.

passages.title: Core of a join
passages.note: The formal proof takes cores of the boundary pullback and uses the boundary equivalence on cores. The manuscript instead constructs an embedding with a section in the opposite direction.

passages.title: Relative slice categories
passages.note: The construction is parametrized by an arbitrary base category. This does not claim full categorical-context inheritance. Boundary specializes to the slice or coslice through the public module aliases at the end of this file.

passages.title: Functors into absolute slices
passages.note: The theorem uses the absolute slice implementation in Section07.Slices. The comparison with the chosen relative slice over the terminal category has not yet been exported.

passages.title: Relative coslice categories
passages.note: The construction is parametrized by an arbitrary base category. This does not claim full categorical-context inheritance. Boundary specializes to the slice or coslice through the public module aliases at the end of this file.

passages.title: Internal functors from a constant family
Subcategory functoriality: items (1)–(3)
passages.note: Only items (1)–(3) have completed targets here. Item (4), preservation of equivalences of the ambient categories and morphism collections, is not covered by these declarations.

passages.title: Uniqueness of dependent products
passages.note: The public Uniqueness module specializes these declarations with the native currying computations, so no extra computation hypothesis is needed.

reverse_only.title: The distinguished terminal anima
reverse_only.note: Same terminal-anima introduction, now stated in the vocabulary axiom.

reverse_only.note: Contractibility reformulates the equivalence to the terminal category.

reverse_only.note: The code assumes separate whiskering unit compatibility; the manuscript derives individual compatibility from horizontal compatibility. This interface has not yet been reduced.

reverse_only.title: Whiskering by composites
reverse_only.note: The code assumes separate whiskering/composition compatibility; the manuscript derives individual compatibility from horizontal compatibility. This interface has not yet been reduced.

reverse_only.title: The two orders of whiskering
reverse_only.note: Derived from horizontal associativity with identity families in the first and third inputs.

reverse_only.note: Action on higher identifications is supporting code for the horizontal-composition functor.

reverse_only.title: Substitution laws
reverse_only.note: Substitution uses the unitors and associator for composition.

reverse_only.note: Acting by an already constructed functor is composition/substitution.

reverse_only.note: Action of a comparison on a term is prewhiskering.

reverse_only.title: Transport of equivalences
reverse_only.note: The former transport lemma is no longer a separate statement. The proof here uses transport across identifications to rewrite a functor as a composite of equivalences.

Naturality of product identity/composition comparisons is supporting code beyond the two displayed exercise formulas.

reverse_only.note: The formal comparison functors act on higher identifications; the old separate item was removed.

reverse_only.note: The same comparison includes its prescribed projections.

reverse_only.note: Include exact Boundaries module header; pentagon/triangle are supplied assumptions in the module interface. The shortened proof groups successive-precomposition checks into its projection argument.

reverse_only.note: Action on higher identifications is supporting detail for compatibility with input identifications.

reverse_only.title: Iterating identifications
reverse_only.note: Explanatory correspondence for the next iteration; this sentence does not open code.

reverse_only.title: Proof of the functor-category criterion
reverse_only.note: Both implications concern the specified induced square, including its matching. The formal proof implements the square comparisons by uncurrying and transposing compatible cocones, then lifting and reflecting their comparisons.

reverse_only.title: Proof of pasting and cancellation
reverse_only.note: The proof maps out into an arbitrary target and applies pullback pasting and cancellation, as in the manuscript. MappingPastingComparison supplies a full comparison of the specified outer mapping cone with the pasted mapping cones. Its proof uses uncurrying and product pasting, including the matchings; no functor-category structure is assumed.

reverse_only.title: Reflecting the triangle through uncurrying
reverse_only.note: The manuscript abbreviates the triangle argument to one sentence. This supporting declaration lifts its uncurried proof; the linked triangle theorem gives the full construction.

reverse_only.title: The inverse of coproduct restriction
reverse_only.note: The inverse of the restriction equivalence supplies copairing. Its separate explanatory paragraph has been absorbed into the copairing construction.

reverse_only.title: Combining mapping-anima-valued expressions
reverse_only.note: Supporting code combines mapping-anima-valued expressions with a common source using the inverse restriction functor. The manuscript no longer discusses this operation separately; it is distinct from the later distributivity statement.

reverse_only.title: Mapping out of a coproduct
reverse_only.note: This is the mapping-anima universal property of the coproduct axiom. The manuscript no longer repeats it as a separate proposition.

reverse_only.title: The comparison target is an anima
reverse_only.note: The target of the identification comparison is an anima. The manuscript now leaves this consequence implicit in the final clause of the pullback axiom.

reverse_only.title: Constructing an inverse through the universal cone
reverse_only.note: The construction of an inverse is supporting code for comparison of pullback cones. The manuscript now gives the two-out-of-three argument in an unnumbered paragraph.

reverse_only.title: The family to be curried
reverse_only.note: The evaluated family is the composite displayed here, now written directly with Map(T,F) rather than naming the parameter P separately.

reverse_only.title: Construct the lift from inverse triangles
reverse_only.note: The two constructions pass between an invertible arrow and a lift to Iso(C), with endpoint-framed inverse witnesses.

reverse_only.note: The underlying-arrow comparison and its two endpoint equations give the whole comparison with the diagonal.

reverse_only.note: The term-level recovery agrees with the curried isomorphism-expression, including endpoint comparisons. The following corollary separately proves an equivalence of the entire identification anima.
